effrontery

/ih-FRUN-tuh-ree/ - the stress falls on FRUN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Effrontery means shameless boldness; insolent nerve.

After crashing the wedding, eating two dinners, and leading the conga line, the stranger had the effrontery to complain about the band.

Example

Halfway through the exam, Priya watched a classmate photograph her answer sheet — then raise his hand to accuse her of copying. Teachers who heard the story marveled less at the cheating than at the effrontery.

Effrontery is stronger than mere rudeness or confidence: it names shamelessness so complete that the person seems not to feel the embarrassment the situation demands — nerve with the blush removed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gall: Gall is the informal word for bitter, presumptuous nerve — 'the gall to ask for a refund after breaking it.' Effrontery is its formal cousin and goes further: shamelessness so complete the person seems not to feel embarrassment at all.

audacity: Audacity is boldness that can be admirable or shameless depending on the deed: an audacious business gamble can impress, an audacious lie disgusts. Effrontery cannot swing both ways — it is always disapproving, reserved for shamelessness that tramples what is owed to others.

nerve: Nerve is the everyday word for daring that oversteps — 'the nerve to show up uninvited' — though it can also be neutral grit, as when a climber keeps her nerve. Effrontery is never neutral: it is nerve with the shame removed, and always condemned.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

humility: a modest sense of one's own place

deference: respectful yielding to others

Where it sits · how completely shame is left behind — boldness → impudence → effrontery

boldness vs. effrontery: Boldness by itself can be a virtue — explorers need it; it stops well short of effrontery, which is nerve with the shame stripped out.

impudence vs. effrontery: Impudence is cheeky disrespect — a smirk at the teacher; it stops short of effrontery, which is shamelessness on a grand scale.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ef-

Prefix — ef-: out of, from (a form of ex-)

Root — front

Root — front: forehead, brow (Latin frons)

Suffix — -ery

Suffix — -ery: behavior or quality

Put it together

Put it together: Latin effrons meant 'barefaced' — ef- (out of) plus frons (forehead): someone whose brow is pushed forward with no capacity to blush. Add -ery, which bundles behavior into a noun, and effrontery is literally 'barefacedness' — conduct performed with the forehead bare of shame.

Use the root in a new word: confront

Use the root in a new word: confront: The auditor decided to confront the manager with the missing receipts face to face.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / disapproving

Effrontery is the formal register of 'nerve' and 'gall,' and it always disapproves. Where audacity can admire a daring rescue, effrontery cannot — it reserves itself for shamelessness that ignores what is owed to other people.
